full_judgment:
Plaintiffs-petitioners have obtained this Rule against the judgment and order dated 8-2-94 of the Court of District Judge, Chandpur in Misc. Appeal No. 41 of 1993 affirming the judgment and order dated 25-8-93 in Title Suit No. 38 of 1993 of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Matlab rejecting prayer for temporary injunction. 

 2. In the suit representative in character has been filed seeking primarily the reliefs as follows: 

 3. The suit awaits hearing and, as such, it is not necessary to go into detailed narration of the facts upon which the aforesaid reliefs have been sought. Plaintiffs case, in brief, is that Government allotted Taka 4,20,000.00 for the development including construction of school building for occupation by the dilapidated tin roof splitted bamboo fencing Char Payali Registered Non-Government Primary School as stands in "Kha" schedule land which was once said to have been in 'Ka' schedule land. But the 2nd party defendants being influenced by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in a meeting held on 15-6-93 to the serious prejudice of the plaintiffs as well as to the party as the locality has taken resolution to construct school building in 'ga' schedule land. After the institution of the suit plaintiffs filed an application under Order 39 rule 3 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for temporary injunction with the prayer as follows: 

 4. It may be mentioned that defendant No. 1 and another has donated the land as described in 'Gha' schedule land and the defendant No. 2 is the Contractor engaged in the construction of the school building. The learned Assistant Judge issued notice to the aforesaid defendant Nos. 1 and 2, the first party defendants, to show cause and also to the 2nd party-defendants, that is, Thana Engineer Matlab Thana, Thana Health and Family Planning Officer, Matlab, Thana Education Officer, Matlab, Chairman, No. 4 Sadullapur Union Parishad, Principal, Matlab Degree College, Head Master, Matlab JB High School, President, Dhanarchak Government Primary School and Head Master, Boalia Government Primary. School as well as to the 3rd party-defendants that is, Executive Engineer, LGED. Chandpur and the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Chandpur to show cause within 7 days from the date of receipt of the notice as to why temporary injunction as prayed for by the plaintiffs should not be granted. In due course 1st party-defendants and the second party-defendants entered their appearance and filed separate sets of written objections opposing prayer for temporary injunction. Learned Assistant Judge upon hearing the parties and on consideration of the material placed by them on the finding that plaintiffs have not been able to make out a prima facie case in support of the claim for constructing the school building in 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedule land rejected the prayer for temporary injunction. As against that plaintiffs took appeal before the court of District Judge, Chandpur. The learned District Judge on consideration of the materials on record arrived at the finding that plaintiffs have no prima facie case in support of the claim of making the construction of the school building in Ka and Kha schedule land as materials on record show that the land of the said schedules are not suitable for making the construction in question and that construction up to the plinth level has already been made in Gha schedule land which has been found suitable by the engineer for the purpose and that the construction so made has the approval of the authority. Learned District Judge has also observed that balance of convenience and inconvenience is against the plaintiffs and that case is in favour of the defendants and that in case injunction is not granted plaintiffs will not suffer any irreparable loss. On the aforesaid findings learned District Judge dismissed the appeal. 

 5. Learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that court of appeal below erred in rejecting prayer for injunction upon pre-judging the matter or the issue involved in the suit in that question of suitability or unsuitability of 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedule land for making the construction of school building is matter for decision at the final hearing of the suit. He also submits that Courts below in arriving at findings about prima facie in support of an order of temporary injunction and as regards balance of convenience and inconvenience of having or not having an order of temporary injunction erred in going into the merit of the suit itself and thereupon in rejecting the prayer for temporary injunction. He further submits that courts below in the facts and circumstances of the case ought to have passed an order of status quo as regards the construction as claimed by the defendants to have been made at the time of filing the written objection and thereby money as said to have been spent in making construction of the school building in 'Gha' schedule land would have been saved. Lastly, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that defendants be restrained by an order of temporary injunction from shifting the school as stands in the land described in 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedules to the building as claimed to have been constructed in 'Gha' schedule land. 

 7. It is seen from the judgments of the courts below and the materials on record that Char Payali Registered Non-Government Primary School, in short, the school, is not in 'Ka' schedule land, but the same is in 'Kha' schedule land part of which as appears from inquiry reports of the officials is a public pathway. It also appears from the judgments of the courts below that from engineer's point of view, land described in schedule 'Ka' and 'Kha' is unsuitable for construction of the school building. It is seen from Annexure-A to the petition that at the time of inspection on 17-10-1992 for listing the school in Development Project it was reported as kutcha bhiti tin roof fencing school. In the judgments of the courts below it has been observed that in view of the nature of the land described in Ka and 'Kha' schedule the committee competent to select site of the school and to take decision regarding construction of the school building adopted resolution to that effect in respect of the land described in Gha schedule land which has been donated in favour of the Deputy Commissioner. The contesting defendants categorically stated in their respective written objection that construction upto the plinth level has already been made and the same is not denied from the side of the plaintiffs. In the background of the aforesaid facts, courts below have concurrently held that plaintiffs failed to make out prima facie case in support of their prayer for temporary injunction and that balance of convenience and inconvenience is against the plaintiffs. There is hardly any dispute as regards the proposition that in disposing of interlocutory matter such as matter of temporary injunction merit of the suit or the issue to be disposed of at the final hearing of the suit not to be adjudged, nor view as to the merit of the case of the parties to be expressed or to be gone into. But for the purpose of disposing of interlocutory matter the court is quite within its jurisdiction in expressing its preliminary view about the merit of the case of the parties as the same will hardly have any bearing on the decision to be arrived at in the final hearing, and in doing so no illegality is committed. In the instant case courts below in considering merit of plaintiffs' prayer for an order of injunction and the objection of the defendants to the said prayer has expressed its first impression view as regards respective case of the parties and thereupon rejected the prayer for temporary injunction on the finding that plaintiffs have no prima facie case in support of their prayer for temporary injunction and that there is no chance of their suffering irreparable loss in the absence of an order of injunction. 

 8. It appears from the papers particularly from Annexure-E to the application for injunction filed by the petitioner before this court that construction of the school building has been completed and that Head Master of the school having been asked to take classes temporarily in the newly constructed school building. In that state of the matter application for injunction has been for restraining the Defendant Nos. 1-2, from shifting the school from 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedule land to newly constructed building in 'Ga' schedule land and also from running any school under the name and style Char Payali Registered Non-Government Primary School in Gha schedule land till the disposal of Title Suit No. 38 of 1993 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Matlab, Chandpur.
